title: [C++] cross-compilation issues with 18.0.0rc0: inclusion of `<nmmintrin.h>` resp. mis-detection of `grpc_cpp_plugin`
body: I'm testing Arrow 18.0.0rc0 in conda-forge. Our osx-arm64 package is cross-compiled from osx-64, and the build fails while compiling utf8.cc because simd.h includes `<nmmintrin.h>`, which Clang says is only for x86 and x64. The command line defines `ARROW_HAVE_RUNTIME_SSE4_2` even though the target is arm64 and I configured `ARROW_SIMD_LEVEL=NONE`. This looks related to the recent SIMD changes.

symptoms_visible: My osx-arm64 cross-build of Arrow 18.0.0rc0 fails in simd.h because `<nmmintrin.h>` reports that it is only meant for x86 and x64.
The failing arm64 compiler command defines ARROW_HAVE_RUNTIME_SSE4_2 even though I passed ARROW_SIMD_LEVEL=NONE.
N0.label: N0 x86 SIMD header selected for arm64 target

symptoms_visible: The osx-arm64 cross-build still fails when the x86-only `<nmmintrin.h>` header is included.
N1.label: N1 cross-build configuration and regression history collected

symptoms_visible: The build configuration intended for arm64 is still compiling with the x86 SSE4.2 definition and reaches the x86-only header.
N2.label: N2 processor mismatch diagnosed

symptoms_visible: After correcting the CMake cross-compilation setup, the `<nmmintrin.h>` failure is gone, but Ninja now says `src/arrow/flight/gRPC::grpc_cpp_plugin`, needed by `Flight.pb.cc`, is missing and has no rule to make it.
N3.label: N3 SIMD issue cleared and gRPC plugin failure exposed

symptoms_visible: The cross-build still stops because `gRPC::grpc_cpp_plugin` is unavailable while generating the Flight protobuf sources.
N4.label: N4 cross-compilation plugin requirements established

symptoms_visible: The conda-forge osx-arm64 cross-build completes successfully when I test the proposed Arrow patch.
N5.label: N5 proposed Arrow patch verified

symptoms_visible: The osx-arm64 conda-forge cross-build completes with the corrected CMake target detection and the Arrow change for using the build-machine gRPC plugin.
N_terminal.label: terminal cross-compilation succeeds

question_patterns: Could you share the actual CMake options used for this cross-compilation?
What complete CMake invocation produced the failing arm64 build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Sure. I extracted the full CMake call from the conda-forge logs. It uses Ninja, system dependencies, `ARROW_SIMD_LEVEL=NONE`, the arm64 Apple Clang cross-compiler, the build-prefix `protoc`, and the rest of our Arrow feature options.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This is actually a native x86_64 build, and I accidentally selected an arm64 SDK directory.
The same cross-compilation options are used, but a few unrelated Arrow components are disabled.

question_patterns: Is this a regression—did the same kind of conda-forge cross-build work with older Arrow releases?
Has osx-arm64 cross-compilation succeeded before this release candidate?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, definitely a regression. Conda-forge has cross-compiled osx-arm64 from osx-64 since Arrow v0.17, and to my knowledge we never encountered this before.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, this cross-build has never completed with any Arrow release.

edges.comment: From c0-c3, all describing the reporter's conda-forge osx-arm64 build: the reporter supplied the complete CMake invocation and confirmed the historical build was a regression.

solution.intent: Diagnose the x86-header failure by comparing the requested cross-compilation target with Arrow's CMake processor output, and correct the conda-side cross-compilation configuration so Arrow sees arm64 rather than x86_64.
solution.concrete_example: The build inputs contain an arm64 system processor, but Arrow's configure output reports `System processor: x86_64`. Correct the cross-compilation setup until Arrow reports the arm64 target; the earlier suggestion about setting only the system name was explicitly withdrawn as the cure.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer derived the mismatch by comparing the arm64 CMake arguments in the shared log with Arrow's `System processor: x86_64` output. The reporter supplied the configuration and log, but the conclusion that this mismatch enabled the x86 SIMD definitions is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: From c5 and the reporter's c6 follow-up. The maintainer confirmed processor mis-detection as the cause of the nmmintrin inclusion, but explicitly withdrew the initially suggested CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME cure. The exact conda-side correction is not stated in this issue, so this edge scores the established diagnosis and correction objective without inventing that detail.

solution.intent: Apply the established conda-side CMake cross-compilation correction so the target is recognized as arm64 and the x86-only SIMD header is no longer selected.
solution.concrete_example: Use the corrected conda cross-compilation setup and confirm that Arrow configures for arm64 rather than reporting the x86_64 build agent.

edges.comment: Reporter c6 states that the CMake bits preventing nmmintrin inclusion were solved, which represents a persistent correction to the build setup. The same corrected setup then exposed the independent gRPC plugin failure.

question_patterns: Could you share the build log containing the missing gRPC plugin error?
Can you provide the complete log URL for the Flight protobuf generation failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here is the conda-forge build result containing it: https://<redacted-host>/conda-forge/feedstock-builds/_build/results?buildId=1060564&view=results. Ninja says `src/arrow/flight/gRPC::grpc_cpp_plugin`, needed by `src/arrow/flight/Flight.pb.cc`, is missing and has no known rule to make it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The log shows that the plugin target exists and runs, but protoc rejects the Flight `.proto` syntax.
The same missing-target error appears at a different Ninja step in another conda-forge job.

question_patterns: What do the installed gRPC package contents show about the plugin target?
Can you check when the relevant gRPC CMake packaging layout appeared?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I did a quick check of our package contents and also found that this layout was introduced in gRPC 1.52. We've used newer gRPC versions for a long time, so the old build must have worked accidentally or through compatibility behavior that later disappeared.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Our package does not install `grpc_cpp_plugin` at all in either environment.

question_patterns: Does conda-forge really need to cross-compile these packages?
Could this build be moved to a native arm64 runner instead?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, cross-compilation is required and cannot be removed. We do not have native runners for linux-aarch64, linux-ppc64le, or osx-arm64, but those are important supported platforms.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: We can switch all affected packages to native target-architecture runners immediately.

question_patterns: How is gRPC supplied across the build and host environments in this cross-compilation setup?
Do the build and host environments each contain their own gRPC package?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We supply both: libgrpc in the build environment, where its plugins can execute, and libgrpc in the host environment, where the libraries match the target architecture. The target plugin cannot run on the build machine, but the build-environment plugin can.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: We only install target-architecture gRPC, so there is no build-machine `grpc_cpp_plugin` available.
The two conda environments use different package cache directories.

edges.comment: From c7-c22, all on the reporter's conda-forge setup. The reporter supplied the failing log, checked package history, explained why native builds are unavailable, and described the separate build and target gRPC packages. Maintainer inspection of gRPCConfig.cmake is reserved for the final solution's engineer inference.

question_patterns: Could you try the proposed patch in a new conda-forge cross-build and report the result?
Please run a fresh osx-arm64 job with the linked candidate change and tell me whether it completes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Thanks a lot! I started a new conda-forge job with the proposed change. Update: it works! 🥳

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched job still fails with the same missing `gRPC::grpc_cpp_plugin` Ninja dependency.
The patched job completes successfully, but takes slightly longer than the previous build.

edges.comment: From c23-c25. This is pre-landing verification of a candidate Arrow patch, so it is a measurement clarification. The reporter states only the raw build outcome; the patch mechanism remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Make Arrow cross-compilation use an explicitly supplied, build-machine `grpc_cpp_plugin` executable instead of requiring the target imported by gRPC's native-build CMake configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Update Arrow's gRPC CMake handling so a cross-build can point protobuf generation at the runnable `grpc_cpp_plugin` from the build environment while linking against target-architecture gRPC libraries; retain the conda-side correction that makes CMake identify the target as arm64.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers inspected gRPCConfig.cmake and found that it includes gRPCPluginTargets.cmake only when CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING is false. Therefore the imported plugin target disappears precisely when the corrected conda configuration enters real cross-compilation mode. Mapping that behavior to Arrow's need for an explicit runnable build-machine plugin is engineer inference, while the reporter supplied the dual-environment setup and successful test result.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c19-c26. The reporter verified the proposed Arrow change in the affected conda-forge cross-build before the issue was marked resolved. Later release-policy and CI-maintenance discussion is intentionally excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify both established causes in the cross-compilation chain: the initial conda CMake setup caused Arrow to report x86_64 instead of the arm64 target and select x86 SIMD headers, while correct cross-compilation then exposed that gRPC omits its plugin imported target in cross-compiling mode.
The Arrow-side fix must support an explicitly supplied, runnable `grpc_cpp_plugin` from the build environment while continuing to use target-architecture gRPC libraries.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the shared CMake invocation and processor mismatch, the missing-plugin Ninja log, and the separate build and target gRPC environments.
Must not present the maintainer's withdrawn CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME guess as the established cure for the processor-detection problem.
Must not treat disabling cross-compilation as a valid resolution because the affected conda-forge target platforms lack native runners.
Must require verification on an affected osx-arm64 cross-build containing the Arrow change before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly experienced conda-forge package maintainer familiar with cross-compilation, CMake, build/host environment separation, package metadata, and CI logs, but not initially familiar with Arrow's custom gRPC discovery internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, direct, and evidence-driven; supplies complete commands and logs, challenges assumptions about supported distribution channels, and quickly tests proposed patches.
